solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drink, long time in large cask (8)

blocks.note: punch is a mixed drink, often served from a bowl
an eon is an age

annotation.surface: Someone takes a long, slow drink straight from a barrel.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma makes "Drink" look like an order; it is simply the first chunk, and "in" is only the join to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is an old name for a big barrel holding around seventy to a hundred and twenty gallons of wine or beer.

entries.clue: Moving stone tablet over from America (7)

blocks.note: the stone of a fruit such as a cherry is its pit
E = ecstasy, which comes as a tablet
O = over, as on a cricket scoresheet
US = the United States

annotation.surface: Someone describes shifting an inscribed stone slab brought over from America.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stone tablet" reads as one object, like the Ten Commandments; split it and "stone" is a fruit pit and "tablet" is a pill.
annotation.definitionFit: Moving here is the adjective for what stirs pity or sorrow, not the verb of shifting the tablet.

entries.clue: Province formerly of one’s birth (5)

blocks.note: a South African province until 1994, when it was merged into a new, longer-named one
the adjective from Latin natus, born

annotation.surface: Someone names the old province where they were born.
annotation.walkthrough: Natal was renamed KwaZulu-Natal in 1994, which is why the clue says "formerly"; the province was named for Christmas, the Nativity, when Vasco da Gama sighted it.
annotation.definitionFit: One word, two senses: a former South African province's name, and the adjective for anything relating to birth.

entries.clue: Shell dropped by strike drone (3)

indicatorNotes.Shell dropped by: a shell is the outer casing, so dropping it strips off the first and last letters and keeps the inside

blocks.note: to thump is to strike; lose the outer T and P

annotation.surface: A military report: a drone strike has dropped a shell.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all warfare, with "drone" as an attack aircraft; here it is the steady low sound, which such aircraft were named after.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a continuous low sound, like a bee's or an engine's.

entries.clue: Old roses you texted about, short of a bouquet (9)

indicatorNotes.about: to move things about is to put them in a different order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
in text-speak, "you" is written U

annotation.surface: Someone texts about a bunch of old roses that has lost its scent.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bouquet" looks like the bunch of flowers the roses make; here it is a scent, as with wine.
annotation.definitionFit: Bouquet is the word for a wine's or flower's smell, so lacking one means having no smell at all.

entries.clue: Tax record lost by lieutenant (4)

indicatorNotes.lost by: something lost by a person is no longer theirs, so the record's letters go missing from the next word

blocks.note: a lieutenant, in its root sense, is a deputy
an EP (extended play) is a record; it is removed

annotation.surface: A lieutenant's tax records have gone missing.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lieutenant" suggests the military rank; its older sense is anyone acting in another's place, from French lieu tenant, place-holding.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: customs and excise charges on goods are called this, as in duty-free.

entries.clue: Sum a union arranged with no opposition (9)

indicatorNotes.arranged: to arrange things is to set them out in a chosen order, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A sum of money was agreed with a trade union, and nobody objected.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a pay deal; the words "sum a union" hold exactly the letters of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The word describes a vote or decision everyone backs, which is the same as one nobody opposes.

entries.clue: What you and yours have as undies (1-6)

blocks.note: the surface means a person and their family; read them as two words, and the same letter stands at the front of each
the definition: a style of underwear named for that letter

annotation.surface: A question about what a couple wear underneath.
annotation.walkthrough: Read "you and yours" as words, not people: a Y fronts each. Y-fronts are men's briefs with an upside-down Y seam at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: Undies is informal for underwear, and this is a well-known British style of men's briefs.

entries.clue: Leak slowly goes around (4)

indicatorNotes.around: turning around means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to go is informal for urinating

annotation.surface: A leak that slowly spreads around.
annotation.walkthrough: "Goes" reads as the verb of the sentence; it is the informal sense of going to the toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: liquid that oozes out bit by bit through a crack does exactly this.

entries.clue: No team players left a single football club (4,6)

blocks.note: L = left
one = a single
Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers, an English football club

annotation.surface: A football club where no player passes, as though each were alone.
annotation.walkthrough: "No team players" sounds like a complaint about the club; it is the definition, people who prefer to act alone.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: people who shun groups and go it alone are the opposite of team players.

entries.clue: Symbolic post in temple, too contrived (5,4)

indicatorNotes.contrived: something contrived has been artificially put together, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone finds the carved post in a temple a bit much.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places the post inside a temple; "in" is only a join, and the temple is raw letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The carved posts of Pacific Northwest peoples bear figures standing for clans and ancestors, so symbolic post describes them.

entries.clue: Millionaires’ houses being televised (2-3)

indicatorNotes.houses: a house holds things inside it, so the word before holds the answer within its letters

blocks.note: drop the first five and last two letters; the five in the middle remain

annotation.surface: A TV show tours the mansions of the very rich.
annotation.walkthrough: "Houses" reads as a noun, the mansions; it is the verb, to contain, so milli-ONAIR-es holds the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Broadcasting jargon: a programme going out at this moment is described this way.

entries.clue: Start off dirty, smeared with grease (5)

indicatorNotes.Start off: the start of the word is taken off, so its first letter goes

blocks.note: soiled = dirty; its S is removed

annotation.surface: Something begins dirty, covered in grease.
annotation.walkthrough: "Start off" reads as "begin"; it is an instruction to take off the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Grease and oil are near-synonyms, so something lubricated or slicked with either is described this way.

entries.clue: Fair about to host a Democrat right in the middle (4,6)

indicatorNotes.to host: a host has guests inside their home, so the word takes the next letters inside it

blocks.note: decent = fair, reasonable
A + D (Democrat), placed inside DECENT
re = about, concerning

annotation.surface: A fair describes itself as about to host a Democrat right in the middle of things.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fair" looks like a funfair or show; it is the adjective. "About" gives RE at the end rather than signalling a reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: Dead is an intensifier meaning exactly, as in dead ahead, so this is the exact middle.

entries.clue: Being full, salesman admitted eating duck (9)

indicatorNotes.eating: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so the duck goes inside the phrase

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
let in = admitted
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O; placed inside LET IN

annotation.surface: A salesman, stuffed, confesses to having eaten duck.
annotation.walkthrough: "Admitted" reads as confessed; it is let in. The duck goes between the I and N of LET IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun for the state of fullness, from replete; "being full" works as a noun phrase too.

entries.clue: Retrograde sport’s turn to appear (7)

indicatorNotes.Retrograde: retrograde motion is backwards motion, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: RU = rugby union, plus the S
to face is to turn towards, as in about-face

annotation.surface: A sport takes a backward step and it is now its turn to show itself.
annotation.walkthrough: "Retrograde" works only on "sport's": rugby union's is RU'S, which runs back as SUR.
annotation.definitionFit: A diver or a submarine comes up into view this way, and the verb spreads to any fact or person emerging.

entries.clue: Swimmer and teacher welcoming time over coffee (9)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: a welcome brings a guest in, so the pair takes the letter in between them
indicatorNotes.over: a thing turned over is upside down, which in a down answer reverses the letters

blocks.note: an otter is a swimmer
T = time, welcomed between the swimmer and the teacher
pupils in Britain call a male teacher sir

annotation.surface: A swimmer and a teacher make time for a coffee together.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, "over" turns the whole of OTTER T SIR upside down, so it reads from the bottom up.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an Italian coffee, an espresso pulled short with less water.

entries.clue: Really tiny amounts charged for a lot (7)

blocks.note: pro = for, in favour of
tons = a lot

annotation.surface: A complaint that a trivial amount was billed at a huge price.
annotation.walkthrough: "Charged" suggests billing; the definition means electrically charged, and "amounts" is a playful word for particles.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: these subatomic particles are minute and carry a positive electric charge.

entries.clue: World on course finally for growth, often flaky (5,4)

indicatorNotes.finally: what comes finally comes at the end, so take the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a world is a planet
re = on, concerning
last letter of coursE

annotation.surface: A flaky world is on course for economic growth.
annotation.walkthrough: "Growth" sounds economic; it is something that grows, a tree. The London plane sheds its bark in flakes, leaving a patchwork trunk.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a tree is a growth, and this one's bark peels in flakes.

entries.clue: Crosses next to outspoken parties (7)

indicatorNotes.outspoken: spoken out loud, so the words are heard rather than read

blocks.note: by = next to; sects = parties, factions

annotation.surface: Someone gets cross beside some blunt political parties.
annotation.walkthrough: "Outspoken" reads as describing the parties as blunt; it tells you to say the words.
annotation.definitionFit: A line cutting another in two crosses it, so the geometric verb stands in for crosses.

entries.clue: Old-fashioned ingredient of beers (7)

blocks.note: an Old Fashioned is a whisky cocktail; a few dashes of a herbal tincture go in
pints of the hoppy British ale that takes its name from its taste

annotation.surface: Some antiquated ingredient found in beer.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen hides a capital: an Old Fashioned is a whisky cocktail made with bitters. In Britain, bitter is a hoppy draught ale, so bitters are beers.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the herbal tincture in an Old Fashioned, and the plural of the British draught ale.

entries.clue: Driver’s foremost sun protection on a coach (7)

indicatorNotes.foremost: the foremost part is the one at the front, so take the first letter
indicatorNotes.on: one thing written on another follows it, so D VISOR comes after A

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of Driver
a visor shields the eyes from the sun

annotation.surface: A coach driver's first concern is a sun visor.
annotation.walkthrough: "Coach" belongs with the driver as a bus; it is the definition, a trainer or mentor.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a coach guides and counsels, which is what the answer does.

entries.clue: Scornful comment retracted saving theologian’s blushes (7)

indicatorNotes.retracted: a retracted remark is taken back, so the word is drawn back and runs backwards
indicatorNotes.saving: to save something is to keep it safe inside, so the letters go in the middle

blocks.note: a sneer is a scornful remark
DD = Doctor of Divinity, a theologian; held inside REENS

annotation.surface: A sneering remark is withdrawn to spare a theologian embarrassment.
annotation.walkthrough: "Blushes" looks like part of the idiom "saving blushes"; it is the verb, and the apostrophe S is only the join to it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a face that blushes turns red.

entries.clue: Girl is taken in by old city bully (9)

indicatorNotes.is taken in by: being taken in by someone means being brought inside, so the first part goes inside the second

blocks.note: Ann, a girl's name
taken as written
Tyre, the ancient Phoenician city; ANN IS goes inside

annotation.surface: A girl is deceived by a bully from an old city.
annotation.walkthrough: "Is" does double duty in the surface as the verb of "is taken in"; its letters also go inside with Ann.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rule over or treat someone cruelly and oppressively is to bully them.

entries.clue: Sports field not opening for long (4)

indicatorNotes.not opening: a word's opening is its first letter, and "not" leaves it out

blocks.note: a football or cricket pitch; the P goes

annotation.surface: A sports ground that has not opened for a long while.
annotation.walkthrough: "Long" reads as an adjective of time; it is the verb, to yearn, and "for" is the join.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be itching for something is to be restless with desire for it, to long for it.

entries.clue: Ties put around grass (5)

indicatorNotes.put around: something put around faces the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a tie is a drawn match

annotation.surface: Someone lays neckties around on the lawn.
annotation.walkthrough: "Ties" looks like neckties; it means drawn games.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary word for turf, an expanse of short grass.

entries.clue: Come to where mourners gather (5)

blocks.note: to come to is to regain consciousness
read as two words: an article plus the vigil held for someone who has died

annotation.surface: An invitation to attend a gathering of mourners.
annotation.walkthrough: "Come to" looks like an invitation; it means regain consciousness. The second half splits the answer as A WAKE.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb for surfacing from sleep or a faint, and, split, the vigil where mourners meet.

entries.clue: Pressure to leave hound in compound (5)

indicatorNotes.to leave: what leaves is no longer there, so the letter departs from the word

blocks.note: P = pressure, as in physics
to hound is to pester; the P leaves

annotation.surface: Pressure to get a dog to leave a walled compound.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hound" reads as a dog and "compound" as an enclosure; one is the verb to pester, the other a chemical.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a class of chemical compounds formed from an acid and an alcohol, often fruity-smelling.

entries.clue: Think of beer and react excitedly (9)

indicatorNotes.excitedly: excited particles jump about, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; "and" joins the two words

annotation.surface: Imagine beer and get excited about it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Think of beer" reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at "Think" and "of" joins it.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal, rather jokey word built from cerebrum, the brain, so it means using the brain.

entries.clue: Reserve endlessly subject to verbal abuse (3)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: without an end means the word's last letter is cut off

blocks.note: to book is to reserve; its K goes

annotation.surface: Someone who holds back without end is jeered at.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase, so the answer is the verb: what a crowd does to a villain.
annotation.definitionFit: A crowd jeering loudly at a performer or player is heaping spoken abuse on them.

entries.clue: Programme broadcast round hospital (4)

indicatorNotes.round: going round something encircles it, so the word wraps the next letter

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it
H = hospital, as on road signs; inside SOW

annotation.surface: A TV programme is broadcast around a hospital.
annotation.walkthrough: "Broadcast" fits the TV programme; it is the older farming sense, scattering seed by hand.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a television or radio programme is commonly called this.

entries.clue: Fans, mostly County supporters (8)

indicatorNotes.mostly: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: DEVON, a county in south-west England, without its N
golf tees support the ball

annotation.surface: Most of the fans are county-cricket supporters.
annotation.walkthrough: "Supporters" sits beside "Fans" as a synonym; it is the golf tees that hold the ball up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people devoted to a team, star or hobby are its fans.
